newsitem.title: EGYPT: Sudan vice-president leaves Egypt after talks.
newsitem.headline: Sudan vice-president leaves Egypt after talks.

text.p: Sudanese Vice-President al-Zubeir Mohammad Saleh left Egypt on Thursday after a surprise visit and talks with Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak which were expected to cover the military conflict in Sudan.

Airport sources reported Saleh's departure from Cairo but they did not say whether he was returning to Sudan. He was the most senior Sudanese to visit Egypt since President Omar Hassan al-Bashir came in June for an Arab summit.

Sudan's Islamist military government has called for mobilisation against what it says are Ethiopian and rebel assaults on eastern Sudan. It has also accused Eritrea of taking part in the fighting, which Eritrea denied.
Saleh arrived in Cairo unexpectedly on Wednesday but the Egyptians kept his schedule quiet.
Sudanese leader Hassan al-Turabi told Reuters on Wednesday that Saleh wanted to ask the Egyptian government about its decision to let opposition leaders use Cairo as their base.

The two major northern opposition leaders -- former prime minister Sadeq al-Mahdi of the Umma Party and Mohammed Osman al-Mirghani of the Democratic Unionists -- were in Cairo for about two weeks. Opposition sources said Mahdi left for Saudi Arabia late on Wednesday.
Relations between Sudan and Egypt have deteriorated recently, especially since Egypt said Sudan helped the Egyptian Islamists who tried to kill Mubarak in Addis Ababa in 1995.
